applied.quote: Court filing fees plus a required credit counseling course before filing
applied.replacement: A required credit counseling course before filing
applied.why: Fact list never mentions court filing fees

applied.quote: Nothing stops a lawsuit during the program
applied.replacement: A creditor may file a collection lawsuit during the program
applied.why: SOURCE only says settlement may lead to a collection lawsuit

applied.quote: Most pre-filing debts, minus Section 523 exceptions like support and most student loans
applied.replacement: Pre-filing debts, minus Section 523 exceptions like support and student loans without undue hardship
applied.why: §523 excepts student loans unless undue hardship; 'most' not stated

applied.quote: Private agreements between you and each creditor
applied.replacement: Agreements between you and each creditor
applied.why: Privacy not stated; credit records identify settled accounts

applied.quote: Without that money, settlement means more than a year of missed payments with nothing to stop a lawsuit, plus possible tax on whatever each creditor forgives.
applied.replacement: Without that money, settlement means more than a year of missed payments during which a creditor may sue, plus possible tax on whatever each creditor forgives.
applied.why: SOURCE says settlement may lead to a lawsuit, not that nothing stops one

applied.quote: The best-known completion figure is low.
applied.replacement: The published completion figure is low.
applied.why: No source ranks how well-known the figure is

applied.quote: Recent spending on credit cards can also stay with you.
applied.replacement: Recent spending can also stay with you.
applied.why: §523(a)(2)(C) covers luxury goods and cash advances, not specifically credit cards

applied.quote: Bankruptcy costs include court filing fees and the required counseling course, and our guide to [what it costs to file bankruptcy](/guides/how-much-does-it-cost-to-file-bankruptcy/) has the current fee figures.
applied.replacement: Bankruptcy requires a credit counseling course before filing, and our guide to [what it costs to file bankruptcy](/guides/how-much-does-it-cost-to-file-bankruptcy/) has the current fee figures.
applied.why: Fact list never mentions court filing fees

applied.quote: The main exclusion outside bankruptcy is insolvency.
applied.replacement: One exclusion outside bankruptcy is insolvency.
applied.why: SOURCE lists insolvency as an exclusion, not the main one

applied.quote: Both paths hurt your score in the short term.
applied.replacement: Both paths can hurt your credit.
applied.why: SOURCE does not say the harm is short-term

applied.quote: Settlement is a poor fit if a creditor has already sued you, because nothing in a settlement program stops the lawsuit.
applied.replacement: Settlement is a poor fit if a creditor has already sued you, because the automatic stay that halts lawsuits comes from a bankruptcy filing.
applied.why: SOURCE says settlement may lead to lawsuits; stay comes from a bankruptcy petition

applied.quote: and the [CFPB says many card companies](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-should-i-do-if-i-cant-pay-my-credit-card-bills-en-1697/) will change your payment during a financial emergency.
applied.replacement: and the [CFPB says many card companies](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-should-i-do-if-i-cant-pay-my-credit-card-bills-en-1697/) are willing to work with you to change your payment during a financial emergency.
applied.why: CFPB says many are willing to work with you, not that they will

applied.quote: A broad exclusion for all settled consumer debt would remove settlement's largest added cost, which we would then weigh against its lawsuit risk.
applied.replacement: A broad exclusion for all settled consumer debt would remove settlement's tax cost, which we would then weigh against its lawsuit risk.
applied.why: SOURCE does not rank tax as settlement's largest cost

applied.quote: No, a settled account usually stays on your credit report for less time than a bankruptcy, though both lower your score.
applied.replacement: A settled account usually stays on your credit report for less time than a bankruptcy, though both lower your score.
applied.why: SOURCE compares reporting periods only, not overall credit harm

applied.quote: The five-year line comes from Chapter 13, where a court-approved repayment plan can never run longer than five years.
applied.replacement: The five-year line comes from Chapter 13, where a repayment plan can never run longer than five years.
applied.why: SOURCE says plans cannot exceed five years; never says court-approved

applied.quote: Income from Social Security or veterans benefits changes the math for both paths.
applied.replacement: Income from Social Security or veterans benefits has its own protections from collectors.
applied.why: SOURCE gives benefit protections from collectors, not effects on either path

applied.quote: Settlement avoids new borrowing, but the CFPB says the forgiven amount could leave you owing taxes.
applied.replacement: With settlement, the CFPB says the forgiven amount could leave you owing taxes.
applied.why: SOURCE never states settlement avoids new borrowing

applied.quote: The five-year line comes from Chapter 13, where a repayment plan can never run longer than five years.
applied.replacement: Chapter 13 repayment plans can never run longer than five years.
applied.why: SOURCE does not say the five-year threshold derives from Chapter 13

applied.quote: A debt settlement program has you stop paying your creditors and save a set amount each month, then uses those savings to offer each creditor less than the balance.
applied.replacement: A debt settlement program usually advises you to stop paying your creditors and set aside money each month, then uses those savings to offer each creditor less than the balance.
applied.why: SOURCE says programs usually advise or often encourage stopping payments, not always

applied.quote: Your savings must sit at an insured financial institution, in an account you own, run by an administrator with no ties to the settlement company.
applied.replacement: If the company requires a dedicated account, your savings must sit at an insured financial institution, in an account you own, run by an administrator with no ties to the settlement company.
applied.why: Rule applies only if the provider requires a dedicated account

applied.quote: Bankruptcy brings a court-ordered discharge and an automatic stay on collection.
applied.why: Discharge is granted unless a legal bar applies; not promised

applied.quote: A settlement program has no legal power to stop that suit, while a bankruptcy filing triggers an automatic stay.
applied.why: SOURCE does not state settlement programs' legal powers
